## One Intention in the Morning, One Review at Night

In the morning, give yourself one modest intention: "Today I will notice one hook before I act from it." Then at night, how'd it go? Look back over the day, and leave out the cross-examining. Maybe there was one you caught right as you started tightening up. Or it's only now, thinking it over, that you realize, oh, that was a hook, and you went through the whole sequence anyway. That counts as progress too, seeing it afterward. For that one, what's the next small repair, or something the Protector could do? And what good came your way today? You might not think of any right away, and then there's a warm moment you'd forgotten about, or something you enjoyed. Perhaps you got a little braver somewhere, or felt close to somebody. Repair whatever can be repaired. Then renew the intention for tomorrow and go to sleep.

## One Intention in the Morning, One Review at Night

At night, before you go to sleep, think back to the one modest intention you set that morning: "Today I will notice one hook before I act from it." Then go over the day and see how it went, and keep the courtroom out of it. You might find a moment you did catch one, right as you started to tighten up. If you only spotted one afterward, once you'd gone through the whole sequence anyway, does that count? Well, it's after the fact, but yes, count it as progress. And as for that one, what would the next small repair be, or is there something protective you could do?

Then go looking for whatever good came to you today. Something warm, maybe. Or just something fun. If you're used to only checking what went wrong, this part might feel a little strange. Maybe you found a bit of courage somewhere, or had a moment of feeling close to someone. Repair what can be repaired. Then renew the intention for tomorrow and get some sleep.

## One Intention in the Morning, One Review at Night

When you get up, give yourself one modest intention: "Today I will notice one hook before I act from it." Then at some point in the day you might feel yourself tighten up and think, wait, is this one?

At night, look back over the day, and don't go building a case against yourself. The first thing that comes up might be a hook that got you anyway, where you went through the whole thing and only saw it afterward. Spotting it counts as progress, even if you're already flopping around in the boat by then 😂. What's one small repair you could make for that one, or something protective you could do? And there might be one you did catch in time, too. Then look for the good stuff you got today, some warmth, or something you enjoyed. Maybe you got brave about something, or there was somebody you felt close to. Once whatever can be repaired is repaired, say the intention again for tomorrow and go to sleep.

## Just Like Me

This one's a way to stop carrying around a feeling that everybody has, like it's proof that you alone are defective. And it sure can seem like proof, when you're in the middle of it. So name the feeling plainly. Just the one, like loneliness. Then say, "Other people know this feeling too. Just like me, they want relief. Just like me, they sometimes make it worse trying to escape it. May all of us find enough support to stay present and not pass the pain forward." That second "just like me" might sting a little.

Only do any of this when you've got your bearings, enough that thinking about other people won't pull you away from yourself. If someone who abused you is one of those other people, nobody's asking you to forgive them, or imagine what their childhood was like. Getting in touch with them while you're flooded isn't part of it either. Breathe normally, and let the wish include you first, then whoever comes to mind.

## Just Like Me

"Other people know this feeling too. Just like me, they want relief. Just like me, they sometimes make it worse trying to escape it. May all of us find enough support to stay present and not pass the pain forward." That "all of us" is a big circle, and it can include people who hurt you. You don't have to forgive an abuser to say it, though, or picture their childhood. Same with getting in touch with them while you're flooded. And "this feeling" is just one, named plainly before you start, whether it's fear or loneliness.

Whichever it is, everybody has it. Saying the wish is a way to stop carrying it as proof that something's wrong with you, and only you. If letting everyone in would pull you away from yourself right now, wait until you've got your bearings. Breathe normally and let the wish include you first, and after that anyone who comes to mind. That part might feel backwards, if you're used to going last.

## Just Like Me

Some people hear "just like me" and brace themselves, like they're about to be told to forgive someone. This isn't a demand to forgive an abuser, though, or to imagine their childhood. It doesn't mean getting in touch with them while you're flooded, either. Only try it when you've got your bearings, enough that bringing other people into it won't pull you away from yourself. You're the first one it's for, after all.

Pick one feeling and name it plainly, like fear or loneliness, whatever it is. Everybody has it, and this is a way to stop carrying it around as proof that you're the only one who's defective. Breathe normally and say this, letting the wish include you and then anyone who comes to mind: "Other people know this feeling too. Just like me, they want relief. Just like me, they sometimes make it worse trying to escape it. May all of us find enough support to stay present and not pass the pain forward."
